title: The sequencing atlas's globe, and the study by the full working chain
set_out: Finish the globe on sequencing against healthy samples outside the atlas, then read the Johns Hopkins leukemia study with the full working chain.
open_at_turnover: The 30 tuning plasmas read again against the 57-cell atlas, aligning on GitHub.

sections.heading: What ran, and how each came out

entries.title: The study by the full working chain
entries.what: All 36 samples of the leukemia study merged from saved pieces and read by the full working chain against the IAM Sequencing Atlas.
entries.outcome: All 36 read: leukemia Met-A in the B-cell column 1.0410, islands 1.3277; cord-blood B cells 0.8620 and 0.7709.

entries.title: The study read again by the complete chain
entries.what: The same 36 with the tumor gauge, the B-cell copies and Group-A added.
entries.outcome: All 36 read: tumor gauge leukemia 0.9922, cord blood 1.0269, the UHRF1 knockout 0.7520. Group-A gives no call: three healthy references leave each only two others for the tare.

entries.title: Group-A on sequencing
entries.what: Group-A read on sequencing bundles: two sealed healthy halves, and a planted 1 % loss written into half of the healthy inputs' own read counts.
entries.outcome: Met on the sorted-cell reading: healthy halves alike (-0.97 %, t -0.772), planted loss found (+7.93 %, t 6.493). On the islands the healthy halves differ (+4.51 %, t 2.231), flagged.

entries.title: The tumor gauge on sequencing: synthetic
entries.what: The distance to the entropy ceiling, counted from reads, in the sorted-cell, in-mix and territory readings.
entries.outcome: Met: a healthy sample reads 1.01136, half way to the ceiling 0.24266, at the ceiling 0.03915.

entries.title: The cell-count floor: synthetic
entries.what: The copies of each cell per site behind every in-mix reading on sequencing, flagged below one copy.
entries.outcome: Met: the copies match share times reads, and the flag falls exactly on the cells below one copy.

entries.title: Higher-order statistics on the sphere
entries.what: Minkowski functionals of the noise maps against shuffles of their pixels.
entries.outcome: Synthetic met on its second version (the first broke the uneven sites per pixel); the real maps are not yet readable, because spread varies across the sphere.

entries.title: The globe on healthy samples outside the atlas
entries.what: 35 healthy samples no build had used, read with the globe against the sequencing atlas and against IAM-Atlas v2.1.
entries.outcome: The range at levels of 0 or 1 was given a counting floor (synthetic met on version 3) and the sample's own counting added; the pancreas samples read level with v2.1, the neurons above it (a three-donor column). The globe's change count is flagged.

entries.title: Healthy samples from another laboratory (BLUEPRINT)
entries.what: 59 public healthy blood-cell libraries from another laboratory read by the one command against the IAM Sequencing Atlas.
entries.outcome: Not met: own-cell Met-A 0.7134 and the islands 0.2924. The islands follow each library's own floor.

entries.title: The common library floor: synthetic
entries.what: Constructed people from three laboratories of different floors, read with and without a common floor.
entries.outcome: Met: with the common floor every laboratory read Normal.

entries.title: Healthy pass 6 with the common floor
entries.what: All 137 healthy inputs read with the common floor.
entries.outcome: Every reading Normal, but the floor overcorrects: the real data carry 0.488 of it. The flag stays off.

entries.title: BLUEPRINT read again with the common floor
entries.what: The spent BLUEPRINT libraries read again with the common floor.
entries.outcome: The islands rose from 0.2924 to 0.8594; own-cell Met-A from 0.7134 to 0.7983.

entries.title: Where BLUEPRINT's own-cell share goes
entries.what: From the Deconvolver's shares in each BLUEPRINT bundle, by sorted cell.
entries.outcome: Mostly to the cell's own subtypes: BLUEPRINT's broad fractions were mapped onto the atlas's narrower cells. Matched definitions read 0.86 to 0.88 own.

entries.title: The 57-cell healthy pass
entries.what: All 140 inputs, including the three granulocytes, read against the 57-cell atlas.
entries.outcome: Met: every reading Normal; the 137 earlier inputs unchanged within 0.0059.

entries.title: Donor traits of the atlas's inputs
entries.what: Each input's recorded sex, age and source from its public record.
entries.outcome: 92 female and 60 male inputs; 29 cells have donor halves of different sex; 6 cells have two tissue sources.

entries.title: The sequencing atlas's guidebook
entries.what: Each tool of the atlas: its origin in sky surveys, its use here, the chain part and its result file.
entries.outcome: Written.

entries.title: Laboratory offsets and covariance
entries.what: What one sequencing laboratory can and cannot measure inside the atlas.
entries.outcome: Laboratory offsets are measured by reading other laboratories' healthy samples against the atlas; the covariance between sites is taken by genome distance from the spectrum.

entries.title: Healthy data from other laboratories, listed
entries.what: Public healthy libraries matched to the atlas's cells, and public plasma sets, kept for testing.
entries.outcome: Listed: healthy blood-cell libraries for 10 atlas cells, and two plasma sets.

entries.title: The range at levels of 0 or 1
entries.what: Sites where every donor of a cell reads exactly 0 or 1 had no width; counting now sets it there.
entries.outcome: Synthetic version 3 met (version 2 not met, recorded); the sphere columns rebuilt with no zero widths.

entries.title: Every atlas input's library floor
entries.what: The floor of all 153 inputs, by the one command.
entries.outcome: Built; identical to the chain's own bundle floors.

entries.title: The megakaryocyte stand-in printed for plasma
entries.what: The summed shares of the four cells pure megakaryocyte DNA lands on, against IAM-Atlas v2.1.
entries.outcome: In every plasma bundle on the v2.1 ruler.

entries.title: A granulocyte column; the atlas at 57 cells
entries.what: Three granulocyte donors built into the atlas, and every derived table rebuilt from merged pieces.
entries.outcome: Built; the 56 cells' values unchanged.
